title: The Detection of Hot Molecular Cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud
question: To detect hot molecular cores in the low-metallicity environment (0.2 solar metallicity) of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) and investigate the effect of metallicity on the chemical evolution and molecular abundances of protostellar sources.

data.angular_resolution: original synthesized beam 0.37''-0.43'' x 0.30''-0.33''; convolved to 0.43'' circular beam (0.13 pc)
data.sensitivity: 0.12-0.28 K RMS for S07; 0.09-0.20 K RMS for S09

what.value: Distance to the SMC of 62.1 +- 1.9 kpc

evidence.quote: The Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) is a nearby star-forming dwarf galaxy located at the distance of 62.1 $\pm$ 1.9 kpc (cite: Gra14).

what.value: Bolometric luminosities (2.8 x 10^4 L_sun for S07 and 6.1 x 10^4 L_sun for S09) and ice/silicate absorption bands

evidence.quote: Their bolometric luminosities are estimated to be 2.8 $\times$ 10$^4$ $L_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ for S07 and 6.1 $\times$ 10$^4$ $L_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ for S09, respectively (cite: Oli13).

what.value: 12C/13C isotopic ratios (49, 50, and 77 for SMC, LMC, and Galactic sources)

evidence.quote: HCO$^+$ abundances are calculated from H$^{13}$CO$^+$ assuming $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C = 49, 50, and 77 for SMC, LMC, and Galactic sources (cite: Hei99; Wan09; Wil94).

what.value: Data of LMC hot cores for abundance and column density comparisons

evidence.quote: The data of LMC hot cores are adopted from (cite: ST16; ST20; Sew22b), where the $N_{\mathrm{H_2}}$ of ST11, N105 2B/2A, and N113 A1 are re-estimated using the same dust opacity data as in this work and dust temperature of $T_{d}$ = 60 K.

what.value: Abundances for a sample of 11-17 Galactic hot cores

evidence.quote: Abundances for Galactic sources are collected from the literatures for a sample of 11–17 hot cores (cite: Sut95; Mac96; Hel97; Hat98b; vdT00; Qin10; Zer12; Xu13; Ger14).

external_data.citation: (cite: Sut95; Mac96; Hel97; Hat98b; vdT00; Qin10; Zer12; Xu13; Ger14)

what.value: Metallicity maps of the SMC and LMC used to estimate local metallicities of hot cores

evidence.quote: We have estimated the local metallicities of the individual hot cores based on the metallicity maps of the SMC and LMC reported in (cite: Cho16; Cho18).

what.value: Mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles (1.94 cm^2 g^-1 at 850 um)

evidence.loc: Derivation of the H$_2$ column density from the dust continuum
evidence.quote: $\kappa_{\nu}$ is the mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles taken from (cite: Oss94) and we use 1.94 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ at 850 $\mu$m

recipe.goal: Image continuum and spectral cubes and extract 1D spectra
recipe.method: Image continuum from line-free channels and subtract continuum in uv-plane via uvcontsub; image spectral cubes with tclean using Briggs robust=0.5 and auto-multithresh masking; apply primary beam correction (impbcor); convolve cubes to 0.43'' circular beam and extract spectra from 0.43'' diameter circular apertures at continuum/line peaks.
key_parameters: robust = 0.5; common circular beam = 0.43''; extraction aperture diameter = 0.43''

recipe.goal: Identify spectral lines and measure line parameters
recipe.method: Identify lines using CDMS and JPL databases based on 3sigma significance and velocity coincidence with systemic velocity; bin 2-3 channels for weak lines; fit Gaussian profiles to measure peak brightness temperature, FWHM, LSR velocity, and integrated intensity (direct integration for non-Gaussian CO 3-2).
key_parameters: 3sigma detection threshold; systemic velocities 163.1 km s^-1 (S07) and 132.0 km s^-1 (S09); Delta V = 4 km s^-1 for non-detection upper limits
assumptions: Delta V = 4 km s^-1 assumed for upper limits on non-detected lines

recipe.goal: Measure spatial distributions and deconvolved source sizes
recipe.method: Construct integrated intensity images over velocity ranges of detected emission (stacking lines with similar E_u for SO2 and CH3OH); fit 2D Gaussian to emission peak and compute deconvolved source size by subtracting beam size in quadrature.
key_parameters: Minimum deconvolved size set to half the beam size for unresolved/marginally resolved emission

recipe.goal: Derive molecular column densities and rotation temperatures
recipe.method: Apply the rotation diagram method under LTE and optically thin assumptions for SO2 (both sources, two temperature components in S09) and CH3OH (S07); for other species and CH3OH in S09, calculate column densities assuming T_rot = 30-60 K.
key_parameters: Two temperature regimes for S09 SO2: E_u < 60 K and E_u > 80 K (or > 60 K)
assumptions: Optically thin condition and local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE)
T_rot = 30-60 K for molecules without rotation diagram fit; 12C/13C = 50 (or 49) to derive HCO+ from H13CO+ with 30% uncertainty

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column density, gas density, and fractional molecular abundances
recipe.method: Calculate N_H2 from 850 um dust continuum brightness assuming optically thin dust emission; calculate fractional abundances N(X)/N_H2 and gas number density n_H2; compare metallicity-scaled abundances across SMC, LMC, and Galactic hot cores.
key_parameters: kappa_nu = 1.94 cm^2 g^-1 at 850 um; dust-to-gas ratio Z = 0.0016; T_d = 50-100 K; source diameter = 0.13 pc; SMC metallicity = 0.2 Z_sun
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission, dust temperature 50-100 K, kappa_850um = 1.94 cm^2 g^-1, dust-to-gas mass ratio = 0.0016, uniform spherical distribution of diameter 0.13 pc
Metallicity of 0.2 Z_sun ([Fe/H] = -0.8 dex) for SMC hot cores, 0.4 Z_sun ([Fe/H] = -0.4 dex) for LMC hot cores, and 1 Z_sun for Galactic hot cores
